findings.title: Frontmatter read errors are swallowed, so the later read-error handling is unreachable
findings.description:
`validateFile` calls `parseFrontmatter(file)`. I read that function: it never throws, and any read error returns `{ found: false, data: {} }`. If a file becomes unreadable or disappears after `preflight`, the user gets a `docType` failure ("frontmatter must declare 'docType: slice-design'"). That message points at the wrong cause. The explicit `readFile` try/catch a few lines later, which throws `cannot read file`, can then only fire if the read fails after the first read succeeded.

The file is also read twice, once in `parseFrontmatter` and once in `readFile`. Reading it once and parsing the frontmatter from that text, or reading first and then calling the parser, would give one read and consistent errors.

findings.title: Fence detection only recognises a column-0 triple-backtick
findings.description: `documentHeadingKeys` toggles `inFence` only on lines that start with exactly three backticks. Indented fences, `~~~` fences and longer fences (four backticks) are not recognised. This matches the ported bash script's behaviour, so it is not a regression. A `## Value` heading inside an indented or tilde fence would still count as present. Consider a comment saying this is intentional parity with the script.

findings.title: CLI tests depend on live repo documents
findings.description: `PASSING_DESIGNS` points at four real slice design files, and the core tests depend on the real 214 design and the real template. This follows the project rule to test against real-world input. The tests will fail if those documents are renamed or edited, or if the guide template is updated. The failure would look like a code regression, not a fixture change. Dedicated fixtures could back the exact-output assertions, with a single real-document smoke test kept alongside.

findings.title: Test file name does not mirror the source file name
findings.description: The testing rules say unit tests are named `{module}.test.ts` to mirror the source. The source is `validateDesign.ts` and the test is `validate-design.test.ts`. This is cosmetic, and the existing repo naming may already be mixed.

findings.title: CLI wiring, exit codes and output contract
findings.description: The command declares `[files...]` as optional, so an empty list reaches the action and exits 2. Usage and template errors go through `handleError(err, 2)`. Failing files set `process.exitCode = 1` after the output is printed. Constants are defined once (`SLICE_DESIGN_TEMPLATE_RELATIVE_PATH`, `DOC_TYPE_FAILURE_MESSAGE`, `DesignFailureReason`). The code uses an `as const` object instead of an enum, and exported functions have explicit return types. There is no `any`. The tests cover the empty-stdout-on-error cases, a worktree-aware template path, JSON output and CRLF input.
